turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. Pop yourself down and I'll grab a blood pressure before he starts. Bit of a queue out there, I'm afraid.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, alright. Don't fuss, I'm only here for a check-up really. Nothing wrong.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Right arm, ta. There we go. One hundred and fifty-two over eighty-eight, and your pulse is seventy-six. I'll stick that on the screen.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): That's not bad, is it. I've had worse at the chemist.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, just logging in, this thing's taking an age. What was the blood pressure again?
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): One fifty-two over eighty-eight, pulse seventy-six. He's all yours. I'll be outside if you want the ECG machine.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks. Sixty-four, according to this. Sorry, what have you come in for today?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Just the check-up. You lot sent a letter. I'm fine, honestly. Waste of your time.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hang on, the screen's jumped. A check-up, you said?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Routine. Nothing doing.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain at all?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain. I don't do chest pain.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. And what about when you're walking, any tightness?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I said I'm fine. Bit of a busy morning, the car park was a nightmare, that's all.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the car park?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, some bloke in a van blocked the bay. Not medical. Forget it.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. Let me just... the template wants me to ask again. Any pain in the chest when you exert yourself?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Pain, no. I wouldn't call it pain.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): What would you call it, then?

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Well, if I'm honest, going up the stairs at home, or if I walk fast to the bus, there's a sort of tight feeling across the chest. It's nothing, and it goes if I slow down.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again, I was typing. Tight where?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Across the chest. Only if I push it, stairs or walking quick. Stops when I stop. It's not a big deal.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long has that been going on?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Couldn't tell you. Last winter, or the one before. Somewhere round then. I don't keep a diary.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Last winter or the winter before that?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, I don't know. One of those. It's been a while, not yesterday, put it that way.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Are you breathless with it?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not breathless. I can talk. It's just tight, then it's gone.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Does it go down your arm, or make you sweaty or sick?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none of that. No arm, no sweat, no feeling sick. Like I said, minor.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any palpitations, heart racing?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Heart's fine. Steady.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Dizziness?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Head's clear.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): What tablets are you on?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): The blood pressure one. Ramipril, five milligrams... no, hang on, they put it up, it's ten milligrams. One in the morning.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ten milligrams of ramipril, once a day. Anything else?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Aspirin. Seventy-five. I take it on and off, not every day. When I remember, which isn't always.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, aspirin how often? The screen lagged.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): On and off. Some weeks most days, some weeks I forget the packet's in the cupboard. It's the seventy-five milligram one.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): And you've been on the ramipril how long?
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Years. The blood pressure's been going on for years, since after I retired, or maybe before that. I couldn't put a date on it, don't ask me the year.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): Anything else from the chemist?
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Just those two. Oh, and last time they did my cholesterol they said it was borderline. Didn't give me a number, just borderline, and that was ages ago.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): Borderline cholesterol, but you don't have the figure. When was that test?
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): No idea. Not this year. They never started me on anything for it.
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Gave up years back. Used to, don't now. Maybe a pint at the weekend, that's it, don't make a thing of it.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right, a weekend pint. And you live... sorry, ignore that, a box just popped up. Let me listen to your chest.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Go on then. I told you it's nothing.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): Chest is clear, no crackles. Heart sounds are normal, no murmur. Pulse feels regular.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): There you are. Fit as anything.

[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm not so sure. That tight feeling on the stairs and when you walk fast, I'm thinking it could be angina, provisional mind you. I need the tests before I'd call it certain.
[SEG0054] person_2 (PATIENT): Angina. That's dramatic. It's a niggle.
[SEG0055] person_3 (DOCTOR): We'll do an ECG today, the nurse can run it, and I'll send you for bloods: cholesterol, kidney function and a sugar.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): More needles. Fine.
[SEG0057] person_3 (DOCTOR): If it hasn't settled, or if the ECG is off, we might arrange a scan, a CT of the arteries. Not booking that today.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): So maybe a scan, maybe not. Typical.
[SEG0059] person_3 (DOCTOR): Exactly, only if we need it. Come back in a fortnight and we'll go through the results.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. If I remember.
[SEG0061] person_3 (DOCTOR): And if that tightness comes on at rest, or it lasts more than a few minutes and doesn't ease when you stop, ring nine nine nine. Don't sit on it.
[SEG0062] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, yeah. I hear you. I won't, but I hear you.
[SEG0063] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep taking the ramipril every morning. And try to take the aspirin daily, not just when you remember, same seventy-five.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): I'll try. No promises. The aspirin routine's never stuck.
[SEG0065] person_1 (NURSE): I'll set the ECG up in the side room when you're done. The bloods form is printing.
[SEG0066] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks. That's us for now.
[SEG0067] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. Cheers. See you in two weeks, I suppose, if the car park lets me in.

spec.situation: Man or woman 50-70 who comes 'for a check-up' and only slowly admits a tight feeling in the chest when climbing stairs or walking fast; first denies chest pain, later describes the tightness. Takes a BP tablet and aspirin on and off. Doctor orders ECG and bloods.
features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Retirement is mentioned, but not explicitly as occupation history.
Prior cholesterol test is mentioned, but not requested by patient.
bad.text: cholesterol blood test (type=laboratory, status=completed, requested_by=patient, indication=previously reported as borderline, no numeric result given)

omissions.text: Negative finding asked and answered: no chest pain.
Exertional chest tightness is specifically not pain: patient said 'Pain, no. I wouldn't call it pain.'
Chest tightness occurs across the chest.
Patient reported he can talk during the episodes ('I can talk').
Previous cholesterol was reported by the patient as 'borderline' and no treatment was started for it.
Planned blood tests are specified as cholesterol, kidney function and sugar; the recorded fact lists glucose instead of the wording actually used ('a sugar').
Conditional CT plan was stated as 'we might arrange a scan, a CT of the arteries' and explicitly 'Not booking that today.'
